steps.text: Preheat the oven to 500 degrees F (260 degrees C). Split rolls open; toast them on a baking sheet in oven while preheating until desired color reached.
Whisk mayonnaise, garlic, and Parmesan cheese together in a small bowl. Refrigerate until ready to use.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add steak and onion; season with Worcestershire sauce, liquid smoke, and sea salt. Cook and stir until steak browned and onion tender, about 10 minutes.

Spread garlic-Parmesan mayonnaise generously on both halves toasted rolls. Divide steak and onion mixture among bottom rolls, piling high. Top each with 2 slices provolone cheese; sprinkle with Italian seasoning. Place tops on sandwiches; transfer to a baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until cheese melted, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Ultimate Steak Sandwich
raw_recipe.description: Make the ultimate steak sandwich with tender and juicy steak and sauteed onions served on a toasted hard roll with garlic-Parmesan mayonnaise, provolone cheese and Italian seasoning. Don't forget to roll up your sleeves!
raw_recipe.name: Ultimate Steak Sandwich

review.reviewBody: OMG! What a great steak sandwich! The garlic/parmesan mayo is awesome! I got away with using Hellman's lite mayo and it was still really good. I can see many uses for it. Instead of round steak I used sirloin and slightly froze it to get the steak thinly sliced. I used a vidalia onion, cut up a green pepper and added that to the mixture. I used a bit more sea salt, Worcestershire and liquid smoke (just another dash). And, even though I had the garlic mayo I did add a bit of garlic to the steak, onion, and green pepper mixture - just a little out of habit. We got some really great rolls for these and the provolone cheese just put it all over the top! Thanks for a great recipe!

We followed the recipe except we used Top Sirloin that I BBQ'd. I let the meat cool and then I sliced it about 1/4" thick. Browned the meat in a skillet then put it in our crockpot along with 2 chopped garlic cloves for 4 hours. We sautéed one onion that was chopped in large pieces. Also sautéed a red pepper that was cut in 1/4" strips. The onion and peppers were added to the crock pot for the last hour of cooking. Served on Costco's 9 grain Chiabata buns. Perfect. Used the juices in the bottom as dipping sauce.
Fantastic, I have never had a steak sandwich that was so flavorful. Our company raved about it. We will definitely make this again.

This recipe was so delicious!! We didn't use the liquid smoke and opted for an aged parm and it was perfect. We tried using steak and it was too tough and you were pulling the meat out of the sandwich. Instead, we were able to buy a roast at the meat counter, get it super thin sliced and the meat was tender and perfect after a few minutes of cooking. This is now a family favorite! :)

We all loved this! After I cooked the steak with the onions, I transfered to a crockpot and added steak seasoning and allowed it to cook on low for a few more hours. It did fall apart a bit, but we liked it that way.... it tasted wonderful! My husband raved and said to keep this recipe on top :)

I used left-over rib eye roast, which turned out to be a BIG mistake because my four young teenage males fought over the limited helpings! The only other thing that I did differently was to add the Worcestershire sauce directly into the mayonnaise mixture. I'm making them again tomorrow for our Friday night dinner with LOTS more beef and onion. You should have seen how the eyes of my young ones lit up in joy when I told them!

Yum! Good and garlicky. The hard rolls were nice and light and crispy. Everyone loved it. Next time I’ll cook the meat in two batches. Too crowded in the pan and steamed the meat instead of browning and created a bunch of liquid I drained off. Then I added a cup of beef broth and more salt and Worcestershire. The meat didn’t have a ton of flavor by itself but the mayo and Italian seasoning flavored it well.

My teenage son really loved this. I only used one small clove of garlic in the mayonnaise instead of three, and it was still pretty strong. I also thought that toasting the bun first, and then essentially toasting it again when melting the cheese, was too much and the buns got too hard. When I made the second round of sandwiches, the bread just toasted when the cheese was melting and it turned out great. Finally, instead of round steak, I just picked up some thinly sliced sandwich steak from my butcher and it worked out great. All in all a delicious sandwich, and I think the previous reviewers were correct in saying that the mayonnaise really made it.

this has been a huge hit at several parties. Used the thin sliced rare roast beef from the store deli. and mada another version using pulled apart rotiseerie chicken.. Also used the dinner rolls you buy in the tray, cut them as one in half, toasted, and spread everything on. then baked it in the tray covered with tin foil. very easy to make a lot!! Wow It is gone in 60 seconds!!

The mayo spread used with this recipe is wonderful! I will use it over and over again on turkey, chicken or roast beef sandwiches. It is so simple and flavorful. My husband really liked it too. I altered the recipe using what I had on hand... I substituted Deli Roast Beef for the steak and marinated it in a garlic and black peppercorn marinade. I then warmed it in a skillet with onions until they were tender. The garlic and peppercorn gave it a steak-like flavor. I think you could substitute all kinds of meats and marinades and this recipe could come out great every time.

So this was over the top delicious. I forgot the liquid smoke, but that didn't matter to me. I started the onions before the beef so they could really reduce down. I didn't have fresh garlic (a surprise to me!) so I used powder instead. That's on me. I sprinkled the Italian seasoning through out and only had jack cheese. Shredded it. On a toasted (with butter and garlic powder) french roll. Can't wait till I make it next time!

The best quality meat you can find, the better. I roasted the garlic in the bulb...sliced off the top, drizzled olive oil on top of bulb then put in preheated 400 degree oven for 30-35 minutes. Let it cool for 15 minutes then squeezed out the garlic after it cooled a bit (cool longer if you need or put in fridge for 15 min) add more garlic than recipe calls for, it's yummy by itself. I didn't add liquid smoke too.
I used a thin ribeye and reduced the amount of garlic. It was an amazing sandwich, will definitely make again.
I've made this multiple times, and company always loves it! Even the pickiest eaters love it!
This sandwich is delicious! I have been making it for several years and it never disappoints!
Delicious! The mayonnaise dressing made all the difference. The only change I made was to use dairy free mozzarella cheese as a topping instead of provolone.
The easy additions in this recipe really elevated the taste of our steak sandwich. I'm so glad we found this recipe.
My husband said it’s one of the best steak sandwiches he’s ever had and my picky 12 year old gobbled it up. Didn’t make with onions since my family doesn’t like them, but this was amazing!
They turned out really good. I will admit I am not a fan of liquid smoke so I eliminated that but my family enjoyed it.
I have made this a few times and it’s a hit with the family. I use whatever steak I find on sale. This top I used sirloin tip steaks and it was delicious.
This was a big hit with the family! Will be making again!
